what: JPG to PDF turns one or more pictures into a single PDF, with one picture on each page. It accepts JPG, PNG and WebP images, and other image types your browser can open.

It is handy when a form asks for a PDF but you only have photos, when you want to send several phone photos of documents as one file, or when you want to print screenshots neatly on A4 or US Letter paper. You choose the page size, the margin and the page order.
The PDF is built inside your browser. Your photos stay on your device.
uses: Turn document photos into a PDF
Photograph each page of a letter with your phone and combine the photos into one PDF.
Many expense systems want a PDF. Put all receipt photos for a trip into one file.
Choose A4 or US Letter with a margin so each screenshot prints centered on a normal sheet.
Put a set of pictures in order and save them as a PDF to share or print.
Combine the front and back photos of an ID card into one two-page PDF.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop images here" or drag pictures onto the box. You can choose many at once and click again to add more. Each image shows in a numbered list with its name and size.
Use "↑" and "↓" next to each image to move it up or down, and "✕" to remove it. Image number 1 becomes page 1 of the PDF.

"Same as each image" makes every page exactly the size of its picture, so nothing is shrunk or enlarged. "A4" and "US Letter" use standard paper sizes. On these, a wide image gets a landscape page automatically. Large pictures are shrunk to fit and centered; small pictures keep their size and are centered, so they are never blown up and blurred.

"None" puts the picture right to the edge. "Small" adds about 8 mm of white space around it, and "Large" adds about 17 mm. With "Same as each image", the margin is added around the picture as a white border.
The tool builds the PDF and shows a green message such as "Created a PDF with 4 pages" and the file size.
Click "Download PDF". The file is saved as images.pdf. If you change the list or options later, click "Create PDF" again to build a fresh file.
features: Add as many pictures as you need. Each becomes one page.
Arrow buttons let you set the page order before you create the PDF.
Keep each image size, or use A4 or US Letter for printing.
On A4 or US Letter, wide pictures get a landscape page and tall pictures get a portrait page.
No quality loss for JPG and PNG
JPG and PNG files are placed in the PDF unchanged. Other formats, such as WebP, are converted to a high quality JPG on a white background.
Choose no margin, a small one or a large one.
Phone photos that are stored sideways with a rotation flag are turned the right way up on the page.

example.title: Worked example: two receipts and a landscape ticket
example.text: Omar has three phone photos: receipt1.jpg and receipt2.jpg (tall, 3000 x 4000 pixels) and ticket.jpg (wide, 4000 x 2000 pixels). He adds them, chooses "A4" and a "Small" margin, and clicks "Create PDF". The two receipts go on portrait A4 pages, while the ticket gets a landscape A4 page because it is wider than it is tall. Each picture is shrunk to fit inside the margin and centered. He downloads images.pdf with 3 pages.

tips: Choose A4 or US Letter if the PDF will be printed. "Same as each image" is better for viewing on screen.
Big phone photos make big PDFs. If the result is too large, run it through Compress PDF.
Crop and straighten photos before adding them, so each page looks clean.
Small images, such as icons or small screenshots, are not enlarged on A4 or Letter. They are placed at their own size in the middle of the page.
Name files in order, such as page1.jpg and page2.jpg, so they appear in the right order when you pick them.
problems: A file I chose does not appear in the list
Only pictures are accepted. Other files, such as PDFs, documents or iPhone HEIC photos, are skipped and a red message says how many. Save HEIC photos as JPG first.
A message says an image "is damaged or not a supported image"
The file may be broken or in a format your browser cannot open, such as HEIC from some iPhones. Save it as JPG or PNG first, then add it again.
The pages are very large on screen
With "Same as each image", a big photo makes a big page. Choose "A4" or "US Letter" to get normal paper sizes.
The pages are in the wrong order
Fix the order with the arrow buttons and click "Create PDF" again.
